props.title: Down to Earth

sections.content: Down to Earth (2001) represents Chris Rock's reimagining of Heaven Can Wait (1978), which itself was a remake of Here Comes Mr. Jordan (1941). This comedy about a struggling comedian who gets a second chance in a rich white man's body taps into themes of racial identity and class that Rock frequently explores. While not as biting as Rock's standup, it follows similar body-swap comedies like All of Me (1984) and Switch (1991) in using supernatural premises to examine social dynamics.

sections.content: The early 2000s saw several attempts to modernize classic Hollywood premises through racial recasting and contemporary settings. Beyond Down to Earth, films like The Nutty Professor (1996) and Dr. Dolittle (1998) gave Eddie Murphy vehicles to remake beloved properties. While Down to Earth didn't reach those heights commercially, it demonstrates how comedy can use fantastical premises to discuss real social issues. SUBHEAD: Body Swap Comedy Evolution

The body swap genre peaked in the late 1980s with films like Big (1988), Vice Versa (1988), and 18 Again! (1988). These movies typically focused on age swaps between fathers and sons or childhood wish fulfillment. Down to Earth shifts this dynamic by focusing on race and class rather than age, though it maintains the genre's core theme of walking in another's shoes. Later films like The Change-Up (2011) would continue evolving the premise.
